claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar structure.
Treatment at approximately 1100°C for 20–30 minutes in a controlled oxygen-containing inert atmosphere will induce in situ oxide precipitation.
The treatment will form uniformly dispersed nanoscale Al2O3/Cr2O3-like particles within the matrix and along lamellar boundaries.
Rapid quenching will preserve a fine oxide-particle dispersion.
The nanoscale oxides will stabilize the alloy's lamellar architecture.
The nanoscale oxides will impede dislocation motion.
The nanoscale oxides will inhibit microstructural coarsening during thermal cycling.
The oxide dispersion will act as a barrier to corrosion processes.
ODS treatment will increase yield strength relative to conventionally processed AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
ODS treatment will improve long-term creep resistance at room and elevated temperatures relative to the baseline alloy.
ODS treatment will improve corrosion performance under cyclic temperature fluctuations relative to the baseline alloy.
The strengthening and creep improvements can be achieved while maintaining sufficient ductility.
The oxide particles are expected to remain stable during extended exposure below approximately 800°C.
Precise control of oxygen partial pressure is required to obtain beneficial oxide formation without excessive oxidation.
Nonoptimal oxide size or dispersion may limit performance gains.
Coarsened or clustered oxides may cause embrittlement.
Performance gains may be limited at temperatures far above the designed operating range.
